proposal.summary: On systems using legacy IBRS, the Linux kernel could leave userspace processes vulnerable to cross-thread branch target injection (Spectre-BTI) because it cleared the IBRS bit on return to userspace, disabling the implicit STIBP protection.
proposal.affected_product: Linux kernel (versions not specified); observed on VMs of at least one major cloud provider and on bare-metal when forcing IBRS on the boot command line
proposal.cwe_quote: left userspace threads vulnerable to cross-thread branch target injection against which STIBP protects.

AV.quote: observed on VMs of at least one major cloud provider

AC.quote: This happened because when plain IBRS was enabled (not enhanced IBRS), the kernel had some logic that determined that STIBP was not needed.

PR.quote: left userspace threads vulnerable to cross-thread branch target injection

proposal.recommended_next_step: Confirm affected kernel versions and vendor configurations, reproduce PoC to show impact (data leak or attackability), and prepare coordinated disclosure with cloud provider and kernel maintainers; backport/patch kernel logic to preserve STIBP or not clear IBRS on userspace return when legacy IBRS is in use.

evidence_quotes.quote: We had noticed that on VMs of at least one major cloud provider, the kernel still left the victim process exposed to attacks in some cases even after enabling the spectre-BTI mitigation with prctl.

evidence_quotes.claim: Also reproducible on bare-metal when forcing IBRS
evidence_quotes.quote: The same behavior can be observed on a bare-metal machine when forcing the mitigation to IBRS on boot command line.

evidence_quotes.claim: Cause: plain IBRS logic determined STIBP not needed
evidence_quotes.quote: This happened because when plain IBRS was enabled (not enhanced IBRS), the kernel had some logic that determined that STIBP was not needed.

evidence_quotes.claim: Legacy IBRS clears IBRS bit on return to userspace
evidence_quotes.quote: However, with legacy IBRS, the IBRS bit was cleared on returning to userspace, due to performance reasons, which disabled the implicit STIBP and left userspace threads vulnerable to cross-thread branch target injection against which STIBP protects.
